title: JPMorgan Forecasts $450B AI Debt Surge in 2027 Amid Plateau
summary: JPMorgan predicts $450 billion in AI debt issuance for 2027 as capital spending hits $1.4 trillion, with growth expected to plateau by 2028.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- JPMorgan forecasts companies will raise $450 billion through investment-grade debt markets in 2027 to fund AI infrastructure projects.
- Total AI capital spending is projected to nearly double to $1.4 trillion in 2027 before leveling off in 2028.
- The bank expects 151 gigawatts of data center capacity to be built between 2027 and 2031 at a cost of $7 trillion.


JPMorgan Chase strategists project companies will tap public debt markets for $450 billion in 2027 to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure buildouts, marking a dramatic surge from $368 billion in 2026. The forecast signals a final wave of aggressive capital raising before AI industry growth rates plateau in 2028, according to a report released by analysts Tarek Hamid and Nathaniel Rosenbaum.


## Record Capital Spending Before the Slowdown


AI-related capital expenditures are expected to nearly double to $1.4 trillion in 2027 before leveling off the following year. The strategists warn that spending growth will decelerate sharply in 2028 as the industry settles into a steady run rate, potentially creating market uncertainty when quarterly outlooks show flat growth for the first time. Officially released on November 25, 2026, the analysis suggests a critical inflection point lies ahead for investors betting on continued AI infrastructure expansion.


The projection contrasts with more optimistic forecasts from competitors. Goldman Sachs anticipates hyperscaler AI capital expenditures rising 50% to $1.2 trillion next year, while London-based research firm Entext predicts growth will decelerate to approximately 25% in 2027. The divergence reflects ongoing debate about how quickly the industry will reach saturation.


## Data Center Buildout at Unprecedented Scale


Between 2027 and 2031, the AI industry is forecast to construct 151 gigawatts of data center capacity at a total cost of $7 trillion. Because most data center projects require multiple years to complete and raise capital upfront, much of 2027's construction is already financed, meaning next year's $450 billion debt raise will predominantly fund 2028 buildouts.


The report notes cautious commentary from Asian tech giants including Tencent and Alibaba as early indicators of the approaching plateau. These companies have signaled more measured infrastructure investment plans, potentially foreshadowing broader industry trends.


## Shifting Capital Structure and Asset Mix


Beyond the $450 billion in investment-grade debt, JPMorgan expects companies to raise $65 billion through leveraged finance and $25 billion to $35 billion in securitized products during 2027. With debt markets approaching capacity limits at this scale, cash-rich hyperscalers will carry more of the equity burden, requiring $2.9 trillion of equity investment over the next five years, largely from organic cash flow.


The composition of financed assets is evolving dramatically. GPU and AI accelerator financing is projected to increase substantially across public and private markets, with compute hardware needs potentially exceeding power infrastructure spending by a factor of four by 2031. This shift reflects the industry's transition from building physical facilities to procuring cutting-edge computational equipment.


## Market Implications and Timeline Uncertainty


The strategists predict a pivotal quarter in late 2027 or early 2028 when capital spending outlooks will show essentially flat growth for the first time. How credit markets respond to this transition remains uncertain, with potential for either relief at stabilized supply or concern about growth deceleration.


The forecast creates a more predictable debt supply environment for credit markets in the near term, even as the looming plateau introduces new risks for investor sentiment.


## What This Means


JPMorgan's analysis reveals the AI infrastructure boom is entering its final surge phase before normalizing into sustainable growth rates. The $450 billion debt raise in 2027 represents a critical funding window for companies racing to build capacity ahead of the anticipated slowdown. Investors face a dual challenge: capitalizing on near-term issuance opportunities while preparing for a market environment where explosive growth gives way to steady-state operations. The accuracy of these projections will significantly influence credit spreads and capital allocation strategies throughout 2027.
